q: For a fixed number of RMSprop steps, why do our N_hid = 20 and 40 mean energies stall at ΔE ≈ 48 keV while N_hid = 4 reaches 7.6 keV — is the paper's monotonic-in-N_hid convergence in Fig. 4.3 an artifact of many more optimization steps, of learning-rate scheduling, or of an early-stopping/best-of-N seed protocol not disclosed in the review?
basis: Our 3-seed sweep at 30k RMSprop steps reproduces the shape of Fig. 4.3 out to N_hid=10 but plateaus at larger widths, whereas the review implies smooth improvement. The gap likely comes from optimizer scheduling and per-seed pathology, not architecture.
next_steps: Sweep learning-rate schedules and step budgets at N_hid ∈ {40, 100} with 20 seeds; log per-seed loss curves; check whether the paper's tightest error bars are best-of-20 or mean-of-20.

q: Does the fact that our best-seed fidelity F_S = 0.99997 at N_hid = 10 comes with a *worse* mean-seed energy than N_hid = 4 imply that the loss landscape develops more shallow local minima with width, and can second-order/stochastic-reconfiguration (SR) optimization — which the paper emphasizes for larger nuclei — remove the plateau even for the deuteron?
basis: The paper's Sec. 3.2 asserts SR is superior to first-order methods for NNQS. In our RMSprop-only run we see clear stochastic trapping at N_hid ≥ 10, exactly the failure mode SR is claimed to fix.
next_steps: Reimplement with a diagonal-shifted SR update (as in Eq. 3.11 of the paper) and compare mean/std convergence at N_hid = 20, 40 against RMSprop.

q: The Yamaguchi-tuned S-only potential we use has D-state probability = 0. For the full N3LO Entem–Machleidt (used in Keeble & Rios) the deuteron D-state probability is ~5%. How much of the *fidelity* value F > 0.999 reported in the paper is due to the trivial S-channel converging fast, versus real work being done in the small-amplitude D channel where information density is low? A truly stringent test is F_D, not F_S.
basis: Our single-channel benchmark cannot distinguish these because P_D ≡ 0. The paper reports high F_D but with much larger error bars in Fig. 4.3 — hinting the D-state is where the network is actually being tested.
next_steps: Extend our Hamiltonian with LAM_SD ≠ 0 (rank-1 tensor coupling) tuned to reproduce P_D ≈ 5%, then re-fit the MLP and check whether F_D reaches ≥ 0.999 at N_hid = 10.

q: The review states (Fig. 4.4) that the MLP has trouble at q ≈ 0 fm⁻¹ because the q² measure suppresses the loss there. Would replacing the standard energy loss with an *unweighted* wave-function-shape auxiliary loss (like a physics-informed neural network) accelerate small-q convergence — and would this generalize to the small-r behaviour of coordinate-space NNQS for larger nuclei where nuclear cluster substructure lives in low-density regions?
basis: Our own optimizer runs also under-resolve q ≈ 0 (visible in per-node residual not shown but implicit in F_S < 1 at N_hid ≥ 10). This is not a peculiarity of the deuteron — it echoes the AFDMC/NNQS discussion in Sec. 4.2.3 for 16O clustering.
next_steps: Add a small unweighted L2 loss against the exact wavefunction near q = 0 (or a curvature penalty), retrain, and check whether the coordinate-space NNQS for 6Li (Ref [92]) gains anything from an analogous small-r regularizer.

q: Every NNQS calculation in the review compares to an 'exact' reference (HH, GFMC, or grid diagonalization) that is itself defined at finite basis/quadrature/imaginary-time projection. Our replication exposed this cleanly: we agree with our exact grid to 0.5 keV while the same grid vs the *physical* deuteron BE differs by ~0 keV only by construction. What is the true methodological uncertainty of the NNQS energy when the reference is not exact — e.g. for 16O where AFDMC is itself an approximation and Fig. 4.8's error bars are Monte Carlo only?
basis: The paper repeatedly cites 'agreement with AFDMC' as validation for HN and FeynmanNet on 16O, but AFDMC's constrained-path bias is not folded into the reported uncertainty. Our replication shows this bookkeeping matters even for the deuteron.
next_steps: Propose a stress test: compute the same 16O with both NNQS-HN and NNQS-FeynmanNet at multiple constrained-path parameters and multiple grid cutoffs and report the *envelope* rather than the MC error alone.
